Meta.title: Diplodoctor — understand your medical reports
Meta.description: Diplodoctor reads a lab report with you: every value, which ones are outside their range, and what to ask. Any AI model, and, when you want a person, a health assistant or a licensed professional of your choice.

Footer.tagline: The health layer of the fleet: an agent that reads the report, and the people you choose to help.
Footer.disclaimer: Beta: running, not released. Diplodoctor gives health information, not a diagnosis, and is not a medical device or a substitute for a doctor. In an emergency, call your emergency number.
Footer.openSource: Open source under the MIT licence. Built in Zürich.

hero.kicker: Open, private, and your choice of help
hero.lede: Add a lab report as text or a photo. Diplodoctor lists every value, checks which ones are outside their printed range, explains what they measure and writes the questions to take to your doctor. Your name never leaves your browser.

example.label: Example
example.title: Ferritin, one value in a report

s2.text: Below the printed range — by arithmetic, not by the model

s4.text: Should we look for a cause, and when do I retest?

how.title: A report in, a file out

add.title: Add the report
add.body: Paste the text or photograph the pages, in any language. Names and numbers that identify you are removed in your browser first.

read.title: It reads every value
read.body: Each value with its unit and printed range, the line it was read from, and a flag that comes from comparing the numbers, not from a model's opinion.

ask.title: You bring it to a person
ask.body: Plain-language information on what is outside its range, questions to ask, and the report in a form you can export and share with whoever you choose.

privacy.title: A medical record is yours before it is anything else

redact.title: Names stay home
redact.body: Your name, birth date, insurance and order numbers are replaced with placeholders in your browser. The model reads placeholders; your browser puts the real values back.

browser.title: Kept on your device
browser.body: Your reports are stored in this browser and nowhere else. There is no account and no copy on our server.

model.title: Your model, if you want
model.body: Free shared models by default. Or connect your own key for a stronger model on your own budget; the key stays in your browser.

capabilities.title: Real today, and what is next
capabilities.lede: Each line says whether it works now. Nothing is listed as working unless it is.

Home.tiersTitle: Three kinds of help, and an honest line between them
Home.tiersLead: Most results need explaining, not treatment. You choose who explains: any AI model, a person who wants to help, or a licensed professional. Diplodoctor labels each for what it is and never lets one pass for another.

ai.name: Any AI model
ai.can: Reads the report, lists every value, flags what is out of range, explains what it measures and drafts questions for your appointment. It runs on free shared models or on your own key; nothing here is tied to one vendor.
ai.limit: It is software. It does not diagnose, prescribe, or tell you a result is nothing to worry about.

assistant.name: A health assistant
assistant.can: Anyone who wants to help, under a name or a pseudonym: a nurse, a doctor from another country, someone who has lived with the same result. They explain, translate, help you prepare, and give their view, for a price they set.
assistant.limit: Their view is a person's opinion, not medical advice from a professional licensed where you are. How helpful people found them is shown. You decide whom to ask.

licensed.name: A licensed professional
licensed.can: A doctor or other health professional whose licence is verified, in the places they are licensed. They may advise, diagnose and treat there.
licensed.limit: Planned. Their licence can be proven without revealing who they are, so they may stay pseudonymous. Nobody is listed yet.

fleet.title: Built on the same ground as the rest
fleet.lede: Diplodoctor is the health layer of the fleet: OrangeCat is its economy, Loki builds it and Solon decides how it is governed.

NewReport.lead: Give Diplodoctor the report. It is sent, anonymised, to an AI model provider to be read and is not stored by Diplodoctor; the result is kept in this browser only.

byHand.title: File it by hand
byHand.body: No reading, but the document and its date are kept together, and the file can be handed to a person you choose. Already have a report file?

errors.not_configured: The free shared models are not switched on for this site right now. You can connect your own model, or file the report by hand.

errors.no_vision: None of the models available right now can read a photo. Paste the report's text instead, or connect your own model that can read images.
errors.rate_limited: That is a lot of reports in a short time. The free shared models allow a few per hour; your own model allows many more.
errors.bad_own_model: Your saved model settings could not be used. Set them up again.
errors.unreadable_analysis: The model answered, but not in a form Diplodoctor could turn into a report. Try again; a stronger model does this more reliably.
errors.empty: Paste the report's text or add a photo of it.
errors.bad_image: That file could not be used as a photo. Send a JPEG, PNG or WebP image.
errors.too_many_pages: That is more than {max} pages. Add the pages that carry the values.
errors.offline: Diplodoctor could not be reached. Check your connection and try again.
errors.unknown: The reading did not go through. Try again in a minute.

Report.sampleBanner: This is a worked example. Every personal detail in it is invented.
Report.notHereTitle: That report is not on this device
Report.notHereBody: Reports are kept in the browser that read them. Open it where you read it, or import its report file.
Report.aiNotice: Read by an AI model, which can misread a number or a word. Check each value against the line of the report it came from, one tap away. This is information, not a diagnosis.
Report.attentionEyebrow: How soon to have it looked at

routine.title: At your next appointment
routine.body: Nothing in this report is outside its range or marked urgent. Bring it to your next routine check-up.

soon.title: Soon — within days or weeks
soon.body: One or more values are outside their printed range. A doctor should look at the report. How soon depends on you and your symptoms, which only a doctor can weigh.

urgent.title: Today
urgent.body: The report itself marks a value as critical or asks for action at once. Contact a doctor today.

Report.emergency: If you feel unwell now — chest pain, trouble breathing, confusion, severe pain — do not wait for a report: call your emergency number (112 in Europe, 144 in Switzerland, 911 in the US).
Report.outsideTitle: {count, plural, one {# value outside its range} other {# values outside their range}}
Report.allInRange: Every value is within its printed range
Report.insideTitle: {count, plural, one {# value within range} other {# values within range}}
Report.source: The line it was read from
Report.checked: Flag decided by comparing the number with the printed range.
Report.notChecked: Flag as the report marks it. There is no numeric range to check it against.
Report.questionsHint: Written from the values that are outside their range. Take them to your appointment.
Report.followUpsTitle: What the report says to do
Report.followUpsHint: Only what the document itself asks for. Tick them off as you go.
Report.whoTitle: Want a person to look at it?
Report.whoBody: Diplodoctor's AI explains. A person can tell you more: a health assistant for their view and experience, or a licensed professional for medical advice. Handing a report to a person here is planned and not available yet: export the anonymised file and take it to anyone you trust, or to your own doctor.
Report.exportAnon: Export anonymised, to share with a person
Report.saveCopy: Save a copy to my reports
Report.deleteConfirm: Delete this report from this browser? This cannot be undone.

Settings.metaDescription: Use your own AI model for Diplodoctor readings.
Settings.title: Settings
Settings.p1: Without a key, Diplodoctor reads reports with free shared models. They have a small daily budget that every visitor draws on, and they are not the strongest available.
Settings.p2: A medical report deserves the best reading you can give it. Connect an API key from a provider below and your readings run on the strongest model that key can use, on your own budget. The key is kept in this browser only: it is sent with each reading to reach your provider and is never stored by Diplodoctor.
Settings.p3: Use an API key, ideally one with a spending cap. Diplodoctor never asks for a subscription login such as Claude Pro or ChatGPT Plus.
Settings.keyKept: Key {hint}, kept in this browser only
Settings.notWrong: This does not mean the key is wrong.
Settings.saved: Saved in this browser. New readings use it.
Settings.tooMany: Too many checks in a short time. Wait a few minutes and try again.
Settings.unreachable: Could not reach Diplodoctor to check the key. Check your connection.

reports.name: Read a medical report
reports.body: Paste it or photograph it: every value with its unit and printed range, which ones are outside it, what they measure, questions for your doctor and a translation. No account; names are removed in your browser first.

privacy.name: Anonymised before it leaves your browser
privacy.body: Names, birth dates, insurance and order numbers are replaced with placeholders in the browser, and you see every replacement before sending.

trends.name: Follow a value over time
trends.body: When the same measurement is in an earlier report in this browser, the earlier value and the direction are shown. Different units are never converted.

models.name: Any model, including your own
models.body: Free shared models by default, or your own key with a supported provider such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Google or Mistral. The key stays in your browser.

records.name: Connect your records
records.body: Swiss and European records as they are held: the electronic patient record (EPD), hospital portals and laboratory PDFs, not only US providers.

people.name: Ask a person, of your choice
people.body: Health assistants, anyone under a name or a pseudonym, shown with how helpful people found them, and licensed professionals offer their help as OrangeCat services, paid in any currency.

licence.name: Prove a licence without revealing who you are
licence.body: A licensed professional shows with a zero-knowledge proof that their licence is valid, and can stay pseudonymous.

matters.name: A health matter, worked by an agent
matters.body: One workspace per concern: timeline, medications with dose and frequency, family history, reminders, and drafts that wait for your approval.

wearables.name: Wearables and exports
wearables.body: Apple Health and Android Health Connect exports, Garmin, Withings and Oura, when a matter needs them.

clinics.name: Clinics on their own models
clinics.body: Practices run Diplodoctor with models inside their own walls and receive patients' files by consent.

Platform.metaDescription: How Diplodoctor is built, what each part does and where it stops.
Platform.title: How Diplodoctor is built, and why
Platform.lede: A short, honest account of the parts, what each one does and where it stops. Every sentence describes code in this repository as it is today; what is planned is labelled and points to the roadmap.

why.title: Why it is built this way
why.p1: A lab report is a table of numbers with a range printed beside each. The hard part for a person is not the table; it is knowing what to ask, and trusting the answer.
why.p2: A language model is good at reading the table and at saying in plain words what a measurement is for. It is the wrong tool for deciding whether 5.8 is above 5.6. So the model reads, and code compares.
why.p3: And only a licensed professional may give medical advice where you are treated. A person who is not licensed can still help, and the product says what each one is. Diplodoctor is built to prepare that conversation, not to replace it.

architecture.title: Five parts, each with one job

intake.title: Intake
intake.body: A text box and up to four page photos, made smaller in your browser. Nothing is sent until you press the button.

redaction.title: Redaction
redaction.body: lib/redact.ts finds names, birth dates, addresses, insurance, order and phone numbers and replaces each with a placeholder, in the browser. You see every one and can switch it off.

reading.title: Reading
reading.body: One route calls ai-kit's complete() over the shared free chain, or your own key. The model returns one JSON object: values, units, ranges, the line each came from, plain-language information and questions.

checks.title: Checks
checks.body: The report schema, not the model, decides each flag by comparing the value with the printed bounds, and never lets the urgency fall below what the flags imply. A value is never shown without the line it was read from.

file.title: The file
file.body: One zod schema is the report: what the model produces, what the browser stores and what Export writes. A file that can leave is a file that belongs to you.

turn.title: One reading, step by step
turn.lede: What happens between pressing the button and seeing the result.
turn.s1: Your browser finds the personal details in the text and replaces them with placeholders.
turn.s2: Only the anonymised text and your page photos go to the server.
turn.s3: The server asks a model, from the free chain or your own key, to read the report. Nothing about it is stored or logged.
turn.s4: The reply is checked against the schema, and every flag is recomputed from the numbers.
turn.s5: Your browser puts the real values back where the placeholders were.
turn.s6: The report is saved in this browser. The server has already forgotten it.

information.title: Information, not diagnosis
information.body: The model is told never to diagnose, advise on medicines or reassure. The product repeats it wherever a result is shown.

honest.title: Nothing is claimed that is not true
honest.body: Every capability has a status in one file, and the pages read it. Nobody is listed, rated or quoted who does not exist.

open.title: Open source
open.body: The code, the prompt and the tests are public under the MIT licence, so a claim here can be checked there.

shared.title: Shared ground
shared.body: Design, models, limits and records come from packages the whole fleet uses, not from copies.

stack.title: The stack
stack.lede: The same column of packages as the rest of the fleet.

models.label: Models
models.value: @bitbaum/ai-kit complete() over the free chain; your own key

privacy.label: Privacy
privacy.value: lib/redact.ts in the browser; CSP with a nonce

record.label: Roadmap
record.value: ROADMAP.md and CHANGELOG.md, read through bip-kit

languages.label: Languages
languages.value: next-intl: en, de, fr, it, es

tests.label: Tests
tests.value: Vitest; the model call is injected

next.title: Where it goes
next.lede: Health matters worked by an agent, and people you choose to help: assistants, and licensed professionals who can prove their licence without revealing who they are. What is built and what is not is on the roadmap, in that order.

Security.metaDescription: What protects a medical report on Diplodoctor, and what does not.
Security.title: What protects a report here
Security.lede: Health data is among the most sensitive data there is; Swiss law calls it «besonders schützenswert». Here is what is done about it, and where the limits are.

anon.title: Anonymised before it leaves
anon.body: The model needs the values, not who they belong to.
anon.d1: Names, birth dates, addresses, phone numbers, e-mail, IBAN, AHV and insurance numbers, and patient and order numbers are replaced with placeholders in your browser.
anon.d2: You see each replacement before sending, can switch any off and can add words of your own.
anon.d3: The table of what each placeholder stands for never leaves your device.
anon.d4: Detection is deliberately generous: hiding one word too many costs a little detail; one too few would send your data.
anon.d5: Photos are not read in the browser, so they are sent as they are unless you cover the details first.

browser.title: Kept on your device
browser.body: Your reports live in this browser's storage.
browser.d1: There is no account and no copy of your reports on our server.
browser.d2: Clearing this site's data deletes them; export a file first if you want to keep one.
browser.d3: Anyone with access to this browser profile can read them.

minimal.title: Nothing kept on the server
minimal.body: The server passes a request through and forgets it.
minimal.d1: The anonymised text goes to a model provider for one request; the server stores nothing and logs only which model answered.
minimal.d2: Requests are rate limited per caller to protect the shared free tier.
minimal.d3: A model provider sees the anonymised text, so read its terms. With your own key it goes to your provider instead.

transport.title: A browser told to trust little
transport.body: The page is served with strict headers.
transport.d1: Scripts run only from this site and only with this response's nonce; requests go only to this site.
transport.d2: HTTPS only for two years; no framing; no referrer leaves the site.
transport.d3: No analytics and no third-party scripts.

model.title: Your key stays yours
model.body: If you connect your own model:
model.d1: The key is kept in this browser only and sent with each reading to reach your provider.
model.d2: It is never stored or logged by the server.

breach.title: If something goes wrong
breach.lede: What each failure would expose, said plainly.

provider.title: A model provider is breached
provider.body: It could expose the anonymised text of readings sent to it: values and dates without your name, address or numbers, unless a photo went uncovered.

operator.title: We are compromised
operator.body: There is no database of reports to steal. An attacker could change the site to send data elsewhere, which is why the code is public and the headers are checked after every deploy.

device.title: Your device is lost or shared
device.body: Your reports are readable by anyone who can open this browser. Use a device lock, and delete what you no longer need.

Ecosystem.metaDescription: Diplodoctor is the health layer of a fleet of products — OrangeCat, Loki and Solon — that one OrangeCat account opens.
Ecosystem.title: One person, a whole fleet
Ecosystem.lede: Diplodoctor is one product in a fleet built to give a single person what used to take an institution. Each product does one job, and one OrangeCat account opens them all.
Ecosystem.unavailable: The list of products could not be loaded just now. Try again in a minute.
Ecosystem.layerBody: OrangeCat moves value, Loki gets the work done and Solon governs. Diplodoctor is the health layer on top: the reports, records and appointments through which a person understands their own body and brings a doctor in.

account.title: One account
account.body: Sign-in with OrangeCat is planned for health matters. Reading a report needs no account today.

pay.title: Paid on OrangeCat
pay.body: Assistants and licensed professionals will offer their work as OrangeCat services and be paid there, in any currency.

build.title: Built with Loki
build.body: Loki builds and ships Diplodoctor and holds its identity.

law.title: Disputes go to Causius
law.body: When a report turns into a dispute with an insurer or an employer, the legal layer, Causius, takes it from there.

account.title: No account needed today
account.body: Reading a report needs none, and nothing about it is on our server. When health matters arrive, the same OrangeCat account that opens the rest of the fleet will open them.

People.metaDescription: Health assistants and licensed professionals: how people will help alongside Diplodoctor, and what each is allowed to say.
People.title: A person, when you want one
People.lead: Diplodoctor's AI explains a report. You may want a person as well. There are two kinds, and the difference is not a ranking: it is who is allowed to say what, and who vouches for them. Either way, you decide whom to ask.
People.noneBody: No assistant or professional has joined, so none is shown. There are no invented profiles, ratings or waiting times here, and there will not be. Until then, export the anonymised file and take it to anyone you trust, or to your own doctor.

assistant.name: Health assistant
assistant.does1: Explains a report in plain words and in your language
assistant.does2: Gives their experience and their view of what to ask or try, for a price they set
assistant.does3: Helps with appointments, paperwork and insurers
assistant.doesNot: What they say is a person's opinion, not medical advice from a professional licensed where you are. They may or may not hold a health qualification, and say so on their profile.
assistant.checks: How helpful people found them is shown on their profile, from the people they helped. You make your own decision about whom to ask.

licensed.name: Licensed professional
licensed.identity: a verified licence, and a name or a pseudonym
licensed.does1: Advises on what a result means for you
licensed.does2: Diagnoses and treats within the licence they hold
licensed.does3: Signs the answer they give you
licensed.doesNot: Only in the places they are licensed.
licensed.checks: Their licence is checked against the public register. With a zero-knowledge proof they can show it is valid without showing who they are. Planned.

People.wantBody: Anyone can offer their work as a service on OrangeCat and is paid there by the person they help, in any currency. Diplodoctor will add the labels, the licence check and the record of how helpful people were; none of that is built yet.

clinic.title: Your patients' reports, read before the appointment
clinic.lead: A clinic can use Diplodoctor the way a patient does, and later on its own terms:
clinic.c1: Patients arrive with their results read and their questions written.
clinic.c2: A patient hands you their file by choice, anonymised until they decide otherwise.
clinic.c3: Run on a model inside your own walls, so patient data never leaves the practice.
clinic.status: Planned. Nothing here is available to clinics yet; it is on the roadmap.

label.title: Everyone is labelled
label.body: An assistant is shown as an assistant and a licensed professional as one. The label says what they are allowed to do; it does not say who is better.

pseudonym.title: Names are optional on every side
pseudonym.body: Patients, assistants and licensed professionals may all use a pseudonym. A licence can be proven without revealing who holds it (planned).

share.title: You decide what leaves
share.body: A person receives the anonymised file unless you choose to share more. Nothing is sent without your action.

place.title: Advice counts where it is licensed
place.body: Medical advice, diagnosis and treatment can only come from someone licensed where you are treated. An assistant's view is something else, and is always labelled as such.
